text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:

- Iran demands 'reparations' from Bonn for losses on connnection with the Mykonos trial, confirms through Tehran newspaper Iran Daily that it plans partial boycott of Germany, British and Norwegian companies.

- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel and former Foreign Minister Hans-Dieter Genscher urge FDP not to push for dismantling draft for German army. FDP leaders expect majority of members in party to oppose referendum on introduction of professional army.

- More than 900 people were killed between 1949 and 1989 trying to flee communist East Germany, research group says in Berlin two days before April 13 anniversary of Berlin Wall being built. New material found in East German archives show that at least 916 were killed and that the number could be as high as 950. Most were killed on the German-German border -- 371. A total of 255 were killed at the Berlin Wall and 189 died in the Baltic Sea.

- Schickedanz takes 20.3 percent stake in Karstadt. Both companies plan to work together in a strategic alliance, Karstadt spokesman says. Schickedanz spokesman says company not aiming to take over Karstadt.
- German Chancellor Helmut Kohl rejects cabinet reshuffle "at the moment". Finance Minister Theo Waigel had proposed a shakeup in several weekend interviews.

- SPD says that Germans have to pay 60 billion marks more in taxes than in 1990. SPD tax expert Joachim Poss says tax increases of 125.8 billion marks have been compensated only by tax cuts totalling 67.9 billion marks in the last seven years. Finance Ministry calls calculations absurd.

- Dispute investment aide for eastern Germany endangers federal budget for 1998. Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt says he plans to talk to Finance Minister Theo Waigel about planned 709 million mark cuts in aide.
- Most German state culture ministers believe solution to debate on proposed new German spelling rules is possible.
- German army soliders admit attacking house where foreigners live in Dresden. No one was hurt in the Saturday firebombing.

- New generation expected at Bundesbank, speculation about who may succeed President Hans Tietmeyer when his term ends in 1999 begins. At least three directorate members to retire in the next two years. --Bonn Newsroom +49 228 260 97 160
